subject.title: [RFC] Multi-Agent Collaboration Enhancement: Capability Profiling + Shared Blackboard + Layered Memory + Token Cost Governance

question: Should OpenClaw pursue this RFC as core generic multi-agent infrastructure, split it into plugin/API-first seams plus narrower canonical issues, or reject the core stack in favor of ClawHub/plugin implementations?
rationale: The proposal changes core state, memory visibility, agent delegation/routing, config, provider cost policy, and security boundaries; automation cannot safely choose that product boundary from code evidence alone.

options.title: Split into narrow core seams
options.body: Approve only small, generic core/API pieces that unblock separately reviewed capability profiling, blackboard/search, memory visibility, and budget admission work, with plugins owning optional policy where possible.

options.title: Core RFC program
options.body: Treat the four layers as a sponsored core roadmap item and require a staged design with storage, migration, security, docs, and proof gates for each phase.

options.title: Plugin or ClawHub only
options.body: Close or defer the core request and ask contributors to ship orchestration, blackboard, and memory experiments as plugins unless a missing core API is proven.

recommendation.title: Split into narrow core seams
recommendation.body: Approve only small, generic core/API pieces that unblock separately reviewed capability profiling, blackboard/search, memory visibility, and budget admission work, with plugins owning optional policy where possible.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the clearest observed scoping signal in related multi-agent RFCs and recent adjacent subagent history.
